applies_why: The judge text does the thing the rule governs because it resolves the Romans 1:3 paternity collision by noting the absence of an explicit textual resolution.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: stating-verse test DG-61 retires — readings: (1) no explicit contrary verse is required, so lack of explicit textual resolution cannot decide; (2) the retirement applies only to contrary-statement testing, not to the need for an explicit paternity resolution.
why: The judge text calls the paternity issue UNDERDETERMINED for lack of explicit textual resolution, which is the retired stating-verse approach rather than chain-against-chain footing.
